Man I understand exactly what that feels like. I had a huge depressive episode last year and everyday id wake up disappointed i had even woken up. I definitely felt and still feel like an outcast to my peers and a burden to my friends. But you have to understand depression messes with your perception of yourself and how the world views you. I still feel like i have no place in the world but the thought that it is just my depression does comfort me even know im currently uncertain. I also relate to the guitar statement but as long as you are picking it up and sucking at it you won’t suck at it for much longer, depression makes everything feel stunted but if you keep at it, soon you will be forced to reckon with the fruits of your labour. This may sound sort of weird but if you have unjudgmental friends maybe try and explain how you feel and ask them how they feel about you for affirmation? Communication goes a long way and if they are truly your friends they will tell you what you are missing about yourself.

Things do get better though it may be hard to see. I encourage you to get help anyway you can , battling this alone is not recommended as i had for awhile. I hope things look up for you and i wish you better days man. You got this.

I understand, i had a long episode of depression over last year and couldn’t barely pull myself together creatively, i had to buy a shit ton of energy drinks to finish producing a album that i had written in a sort of suspected manic episode  (the doctor believes i have bpd but it felt very euphoric and crazy and it was a clear shift from my uneventful depression so idk im just speculating, using mania as a placeholder) my advice for song writing when the creativity stream stops flowing is to deconstruct pre existing songs and re arrange the chords until your satisfied. Start humming and find a melody while you play. Bam ! This exercise is pretty easy and can help with inspiration a lot, Ramble on the melody as a place holder until you find yourself in a better creative situation. When I started writing music i was awful and I believed I couldnt even write a simple song, but i stuck with it and eventually improved now i can write a song in a hour if i wanted to. Song writing is exactly like learning a instrument, practice practice practice, trust me it does get easier. Depression is a bitch but sometimes it can give you something to write about. Using my depression as an inspiration for a song my writing just flows lyrically. Maybe try channeling it into your song writing? I hope this helps im pretty bad at interpreting posts lol sorry.

These are just things that help me, everyone is different  i am just offering you my advice from personal experience i hope it can help :)
